facts.fact: Newsmada reports ProPFR digitised land data in the Analamanga region and piloted an interconnected land information system linking topographic circumscriptions and land offices.

PRODUIR reports that after dematerialising legal-status certificates and topographic plans for Antananarivo, an automatic information kiosk entered public service on 7 July 2025 at the Tana-ville land office, issuing registration and legal-status certificates and individual plans.

facts.fact: Newsmada reports Madagascar's land system still rests on century-old, often incomplete or deteriorated archives, and that South Korea intends to support digitising land data.

Madagascar's decentralisation and land-planning ministry said in April 2025 that its land information system (SIF) will be deployed progressively in five pilot regions under National Land Programme II.

systems.owner: Ministry of Decentralisation and Land Planning

facts.fact: FAO says Madagascar's World Bank-backed CASEF project has certified 1.1 million parcels with QR-coded certificates linked to a digital version that will be stored in a national register once the system is fully implemented, with computers supplied to over 400 municipal land offices.

systems.owner: Government of Madagascar with World Bank
